title: First band job: Pep Wallace, Baby Dodds, and clowning with the horn
summary: He forms his first band with Roy Palmer, Baby Dodds on a makeshift drum kit, and plays his first concert and dance mostly clowning.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: And he laughed. He says, no. He says, Joe Oliver is all right. Freddie Kepler's all right. He said, but you want to learn music. Oh, I said, I'll learn all right. He said, but you better watch yourself. And he couldn't talk and he went on down the street. Well, every evening he'd pass by there going home, not late at night, but it'd be in the early part of the night. I'd see him maybe three or four times a week. So Roy knew music. But Roy never coaxed me with the music end of it. Roy, to teach me how to play, he'd bring his trombone down there. And he'd tell me to follow him. Now the music, he figured I could pick up when I got ready. But I liked music. I liked the idea of music. So after about a week's practice me and Roy had, Freddie Kepler gave Roy a job back Tulane Avenue somewhere, somewhere around Tulane, Laperone, somewhere back in there, see? And it was a concert and a dance afterwards. And at them times, as I learned in later years, that dance bands hadn't been out very long. You see, that was around 1909, 1910. Well, they hadn't been out very long. And Roy got the band together. We got a fellow by the name of Pep Wallace on bass, Roy Palmer on trombone, myself on conant, and didn't even have a case for it. I wrapped it up in newspaper and kept it on the job that night. And I couldn't blow it. It didn't take no chance of blowing it because I guess I had more of a idea of clowning. And it was something that the people had never seen. And I always did believe in playing, like you see Lionel Hampton, them doing, say something when they do. It's like Dots used to do. Dots would sit by the drums and say, like that all night long, see? Couldn't tell what he was doing. Well, that was mine. Was that the drummer? Baby Dots, yeah. Oh, Baby Dots. Yeah. I got Baby Dots on drums, Pep Wallace on bass, Rob Smith on guitar, Roy Palmer on trombone, myself on conant, didn't use no piano. Seven pieces. And Sidney Bechet on climbing. Well, we got him a pair of long pants, see, because we decided all old musicians that was in long pants went in and played. We'd get long pants for the youngsters. So many of the youngsters. I had to get long pants for Baby Dots. I had to carry his drums, see, because he was very small. And whenever we went anywhere on a job, I had to carry his drum because his drum was about that high. You know how high the brass band drums would be? Would they rope someone and spit on them and pull them? Well, that was his first drum. And to eliminate the load, we didn't use no snare drum. We used a banjo head, broke the head off of a banjo and tied it in a chair. And Baby Dots played on that. That's what he played on. And the pedal was a flow pedal. The Ludwig, the leadies wasn't out. The leadies, I think, was the overhead pedal, the last pedal was out. Was the pedals up? Did you see the Ludwig pedals on the flow? Well, the Ludwig pedals only come up just to the beater. The cymbal attached onto the bass drum. You don't see nothing like that now. We had a cymbal attached onto the bass drum. I didn't see that, I remember that. Well, that's what we had, and that's what I hated to carry, was that cymbal. And that flow pedal, I think it was a Ludwig. You see, Ludwig come ahead of Ludwig in later years when they come up with that overhead pedal. Down here it just had a piece of wood, and it come from a spring from the top, and the cymbal set on the top of your drum. You understand? I'm saying pictures of him. Yeah. And we went out to that night and played that concert. They had a girl playing the accent. Then it got so good until all the boys in the band and Roy, we went and set in with this girl, was playing this concert. And the people just admired the band. After then, there was nothing I could do. I couldn't play, so I just held the horn in my hand and walked on the music stand in front of the band, and clapped my hands. The rest of the band played. Now that was Freddie Kepler's job. That was a man, they'd been used to Freddie Kepler's band. So from the strength of that job, we got three more jobs. Two or three more jobs that we practically made good on. And then about, well it took me about, somewhere else along about six weeks, and I practically got in the band and played. I put the horn, but whatever I couldn't play along, that's how I ruined my lift. You can't see it now because I've been Oliver. But I started in the center of my mouth.
